title: Customer-priority buckets and automated swapback safety for model catalog
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers increasingly request rapid model additions, version pins, and controlled deprecations. Current intake queues are FIFO-ish and don't systematically protect high-impact customers from quality regressions or provide a predictable swapback (rollback) path when a new model variant causes regressions.

Goal: Define and implement a customer-priority bucketizer plus an automated swapback safety mechanism that ties intake priority to contractual SLAs, runs targeted eval sampling during onboarding canaries, and enables automatic or semi-automatic rollback (swapback) when predefined regression signals exceed thresholds. We want predictable exposure windows for enterprise customers, audit trails, and a minimal-ops rollback path.

Scope:
- Priority buckets (Platinum/Gold/Silver) driven by contract tiers and risk signals.
- Eval sampling plan and workload mirrors for each bucket (traffic split, prompt sets).
- Swapback triggers (quality regressions, latency SLO breaches, cost anomalies) and automated rollback workflow.
- Console UX surfaces: per-request status, exposure window, rollback history, and audit log links.
- Documentation and runbook for Solutions/SEs and Customer Success.

Out of scope: model training, large-scale mitigation beyond catalog controls (e.g., global routing changes).
acceptance_criteria: Bucket definitions documented and approved by GTM and Legal
Canary eval harness integrated with catalog onboarding flow and can run on per-request sample sets
Automated swapback policy implemented with a configurable set of triggers and a safe fallback model list
Console shows per-customer exposure window, current canary metrics, and a rollback action button for authorized roles
Runbook created and linked; 2 SRE drills carried out with documented outcomes
comments: 2025-03-02 - Asha K: Initial proposal posted. Asked Solutions Eng to validate sample prompts for enterprise customers (esp. financial/legal).
2025-03-04 - Priya Menon (Sales Eng): Added customer examples where swapback would have avoided outages. Requested a short SLA window definition for Platinum customers.
2025-03-05 - Liam O'Connor: Scoped a minimal implementation — bucketizer + canary evaluator + a policy-driven swapback. Flagging ENG-27441 for runtime hooks (kv-cache & routing).
2025-03-07 - Design review (Kara): UX mockups attached in Confluence, recommended a read-only audit panel for lower tiers to avoid data leakage.

2025-03-10 - Legal (R. Gomez): Reviewed contract language proposal; requested explicit customer opt-in for auto-rollback when liability could be affected. Added requirement for audit trail retention to meet compliance requests.
2025-03-12 - PM sync: Agreed to MVP scope (buckets + canary sampling + automated swapback with manual approval gating for Silver). Assigned ENG to build hooks and Console to show exposure window.
decision_log: 2025-03-06 - Decided to center bucket definitions on contractual terms (SLA, exposure limit) rather than purely on traffic volume to simplify GTM alignment.

2025-03-09 - Chose three default trigger categories for swapback: quality regression (>5% drop on eval set), latency SLO breach (>50ms P95 delta), cost anomaly (>30% increase in per-token compute cost).
2025-03-11 - Opted for safe-fallback list: maintain up to three pre-approved model variants per customer that can be used immediately on swapback.
